mechanism: Confirmed exactly as written, and the drive sites make it worse than the record says. Core's SigNetParams (refs/bitcoin/src/kernel/chainparams.cpp:437-511) treats the challenge as the SEED of the whole chain identity: vFixedSeeds and vSeeds are cleared at :439-441 and the two public signet DNS seeds are re-added only in the no-custom-challenge branch (:443-445); the custom branch (:458-465) zeroes nMinimumChainWork, zeroes defaultAssumeValid and zeroes the assumed sizes/chainTxData; options.seeds (ReadSigNetArgs, chainparams.cpp:27-29, from -signetseednode) REPLACES vSeeds outright at :471-473; and pchMessageStart is the first 4 bytes of sha256d of the SERIALIZED challenge (:507-511), so every custom signet is a separate p2p network. Only the genesis block is NOT derived (CreateGenesisBlock at :514 takes fixed arguments), so our unchanged genesis is correct and the record's mention of it is not a defect. Ours: -signetchallenge is a real registered option (src/config-options.lisp:216) whose only effect is (setf bl.val:*signet-challenge*); the :signet row of src/util/chainparams.lisp:257-296 hardcodes magic 0A03CF40, the two public signet DNS seeds, minimum-chain-work 0x...b463ea0a4b8, the public signet assumevalid and two public-signet assumeutxo entries, and nothing recomputes any of them. -signetseednode is a :core-only name (src/config-options.lisp:451). Executed both as a pure resolve and through the real startup path: after INIT-NODE on :signet with a custom challenge in force, bl.ser:*network-magic* (set at src/node/init.lisp:44) is still the public signet's and bl.net:*dns-seeds* (set at src/node/init.lisp:46) is still the two public signet seeds, while bl.val:signet-challenge-for-network correctly returns the custom challenge to the block-solution check.
consequence: A node an operator has configured for a private signet is on the PUBLIC signet's p2p network: it queries the public signet DNS seeds, dials public signet nodes and completes handshakes with them (the magic on the wire is 0A03CF40), announcing a private test network's node into the public one, while the peer named by -signetseednode is discarded. The symmetric half is that it cannot reach its own network at all: a Bitcoin Core node on the same custom signet speaks the DERIVED magic (7ec653a5 for the challenge probed), so the two never complete a handshake. It also cannot follow its own chain: the inherited nMinimumChainWork is the public signet's accumulated work (12,396,326,331,576), which a fresh private signet will never exceed, so the node stays in IBD, and the inherited assumevalid names a block the custom chain does not contain. Refuter check on the warning line: the startup WARN (src/node/init.lisp:1664-1668) names -signetseednode and NOT -signetchallenge, because -signetchallenge is a real implemented option; so the operator is told only that the seed node was dropped and is given no hint that the magic, seeds, minimum chain work and assumevalid were never derived. Refuter check on reachability: a custom signet is a fully reachable configuration on this node -- the option is registered, the node starts on :signet, and check-signet-block-solution validates against the custom challenge -- so this is a supported mode that is broken, not an unreachable one. -minimumchainwork and -assumevalid do exist as real options and can paper over two of the four by hand; the magic and the seed list cannot be overridden by any option.
evidence: Probe build/ga11v/p-signet.lisp (worktree fix/ga11v-options-s2a, warm image). fix_shape: Make the :signet row a TEMPLATE that a custom challenge instantiates, the way Core makes SigNetParams a constructor over SigNetOptions rather than a table. Promote -signetseednode to a real repeatable option (Core reads it with GetArgs, so it is a list) alongside the existing -signetchallenge, and add one function that takes the resolved challenge and seed list and returns the chain-params for this run: with no custom challenge it returns today's row verbatim; with one it copies the row and overwrites magic with the first four bytes of sha256d of the CompactSize-prefixed challenge, minimum-chain-work with 0, assumevalid-hex with NIL, assumeutxo with the empty list, fixed-seeds with the empty list, and dns-seeds with the -signetseednode list (empty when none was given -- Core leaves vSeeds cleared, it does not fall back to the public seeds). Call it from the same place -signetchallenge is applied today, before init-node reads network-magic and network-dns-seeds, so both process globals and every later reader see the derived values; keep the existing -minimumchainwork / -assumevalid overrides winning over the derived zeroes, matching Core's later ApplyArgsManOptions ordering. Add a positive control that the derivation reproduces 0A03CF40 from the default challenge, so a future change cannot make it vacuous, and a test that two different challenges give two different magics.
